text:
Priya (AE): Heads up — ACME legal pushed back with redlines on price protection & MFN. They want MFN for 12 months and a cap removal on future promotional pricing.
Kevin (Sales): Ugh. Do they mean no one can beat their price or that we must retroactively credit?
Jordan (Legal): They submitted this clause: "Customer shall receive the most favorable pricing offered by Redwood to any third party for substantially similar services during the 12 month term." No explicit carveouts.
Alex S: That language is broad — could force retro credits if we later run a limited promo for a different segment.
Maya R: What's the typical carve we use? I thought we kept MFN but excluded promotional/limited trials and MSP channel deals.
Jordan (Legal): Right. Suggest redline: add carveouts for (i) time-limited promotions <30 days, (ii) channel/partner offers, and (iii) enterprise committed discounts tied to minimum ARR.
Priya (AE): ACME is asking for POC pricing: 50% off first 3 months. If we accept MFN as-is they could argue that promo becomes baseline for 12 months.
Kevin (Sales): Can we offer the POC discount but document it as a one-off "POC concession" with explicit no-MFN effect?
Jordan (Legal): We can, but they often push back. Proposed contract language: 
```
"Notwithstanding any MFN provision, the parties agree that (i) POC concessions described in Schedule A are one-time, non-recurring, and do not constitute a basis for MFN comparisons, and (ii) time-limited promotional offers of 30 days or less are excluded from MFN."
```
Alex S: Also want a cap on exposure: recommend adding a cumulative refund/credit cap equal to 3 months of invoiced fees for any retroactive adjustments.
Maya R: From pricing ops perspective, unlimited retro credits = no-go. Need an explicit monetary cap and clear trigger events.
Priya (AE): ACME is pushing hard for market parity clause — typical buyer play. They threatened legal escalation if we remove MFN entirely.
Emma (CFO): If we add a cap, what's the worst-case cost? Run scenario: assume we give a later 20% promo to same cohort, compute retro credits. But 3-month cap seems reasonable.
Kevin (Sales): For deal economics, POC concession + 12 month MFN with carveouts + 3-month credit cap keeps margin sane. I can sell that internally.
Jordan (Legal): I'll draft the redline: MFN with explicit carveouts for POCs, promos <30 days, channel/partner, and commits, plus credit cap = 3x monthly fee. I'll tag it as high-priority for ACME.
Priya (AE): Please cc me when sent. Also note we need Deal Desk approval for the reduced POC pricing and the commit terms.
DeployBot: Deal Desk queue updated: ticket #DD-4921 created by Priya (AE) for ACME — awaiting pricing approval.
Kevin (Sales): @Emma could you OK a one-time POC concession of 50% for 3 months under these legal carveouts?
Emma (CFO): Approve POC concession under conditions: (1) written carveout from MFN, (2) refund cap = 3 months, (3) min committed ARR after POC >= $180k/yr or automatic reversion to standard list pricing.
Priya (AE): Noted. I'll push that to ACME and request the original MFN redline be modified to include these items.
Jordan (Legal): Drafting now. ETA 2 hours.
Alex S: Also flag to Product: if ACME demands feature parity MFN we need to limit to pricing only — not feature availability.
Maya R: Good call. Add line: MFN applies to pricing for substantially similar services, excluding beta/feature rollouts.
Priya (AE): Thanks all — will update thread after Jordan sends redline.
Kevin (Sales): Thanks. :thumbsup:
